problem_solved.name: Hyperinvariant-subspace problem (HSP) on separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space
problem_solved.as_posed: Does every bounded nonscalar operator T on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space have a nontrivial closed subspace invariant under every operator commuting with T? (Douglas-Pearcy 1972; Kim-Pearcy-Shields 1976; Radjavi-Rosenthal problem lists.) Open in particular for quasinilpotent operators.
problem_solved.answer_claimed: NO: a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent counterexample on every such space (two independent constructions).
problem_solved.relation_to_ISP: HSP is a strengthening of the invariant-subspace problem (ISP) on the 'positive' side: an operator without invariant subspaces has no hyperinvariant ones, so an ISP counterexample would be an HSP counterexample, not conversely. The counterexample here has MANY ordinary invariant subspaces (L^2(X;K_{>=h}) in BI, conclusion.tex:27-32; in IP, invariant subspaces exist but their projections lie outside R_theta). Hence the ISP on Hilbert space is NOT settled by this family; Enflo's 2023 claimed positive ISP solution (arXiv 2305.15442) is not contradicted. The Kerchy-Pearcy claimed equivalence HSP<=>ISP (arXiv 2503.13005) was withdrawn; if both it and this family were correct, ISP would fail -- BI says the problems 'must remain distinct' (introduction.tex:114-117).
other_problems_answered: Transitive algebra problem (is every unital transitive, WOT/SOT-closed operator algebra dense in B(H)?) -- negatively, via the commutant (BI introduction.tex:79-82). Strictly a corollary of the HSP counterexample.

Zhu-Fang-Shi question (Math. Scand. 120 (2017), p.264, after Prop. 5.7) on affiliated invariant subspaces of u f(v) with FK determinant zero -- negatively, at every prescribed irrational angle (IP Thm 1.1).
Invariant-subspace problem relative to the hyperfinite II_1 factor (Haagerup-Schultz open case: Brown measure a point mass) -- negatively (IP; product model has Brown measure delta_0).

Refutes the hyperinvariant assertion of Cho-Ko-Lee 2017 Cor. 2.8 (IP Remark 1.5). If correct, it also refutes the claimed AFFIRMATIVE HSP solutions of Garayev (arXiv 2607.16373, July 2026) and Sa Ge Lee (arXiv 2306.13940) (search snippets only).

main_statement.latex: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:direct-algebra} Every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space admits a nonzero bounded norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace. Its commutant is a proper strongly closed unital transitive complex operator algebra. \end{corollary}
main_statement.paraphrase: S = direct integral over the 2-adic odometer of compact, unicellular (Domar-type) bilateral weighted shifts with quadratically decaying log-weights; a contraction V in {S}' maps the tail K_{>=h} at x densely onto K_{>=h-1} at x+1. Any {S}'-invariant subspace is a field of tails with label s(x+1) <= s(x)-1, impossible on a probability space unless trivial.

companion_statement.latex: For every irrational theta in (0,1) there exists a continuous function f:T->[0,1] such that f^{-1}({0})={1}, int_T log f dm = -infinity, and every projection p in R_theta satisfying (1-p)Uf(V)p=0 is either 0 or 1.
companion_statement.consequence: Cor 1.4 (00-introduction.tex:94-110): HSP counterexample via Dykema's Prop 2.1 (hyperinvariant projections of T in M lie in M).

D.max_item: B16+B17+B18 (E1): the two-ended-drift weights and the bounded backward intertwiner across fibers of the odometer

evidence.quote: Our additional task is to link the fibers by a bounded commuting operator that moves their invariant tails backward. Opposite logarithmic changes at the two ends of the bilateral sequence make this possible

caveats: Every ingredient except the coupling device is known (Domar-type unicellular bilateral shifts; odometer; recurrence/descent; decomposable operators).

Once one decides to look for a decomposable model whose commutant contains a fiber-moving operator, commutation forces the coefficient recurrence (closed form w_{j-1}(theta x)/w_j(x)); the discovery is the weight design making it bounded, so the pivot may be short.

The II_1-factor route (Dykema Prop 2.1; commutant of T in M contains JMJ, which includes fiber-moving unitaries) is a known route for this problem type; BI can be read as a hand-built decomposable shadow of that route. In the same release the companion uses that route.
Unrefereed; no reasoning trace; correctness of a 50-year-old problem's resolution rests heavily on the Lean check.

steps.claim: Domar-type criterion: two-ended log-convex/concave weights with quadratic growth (a>log 3) give a bilateral weighted shift whose closed invariant subspaces are exactly tails.
2-adic weights a_k^pm with residue corrections +-D T_m: every fiber satisfies step 1; uniform power bound gives norm-quasinilpotence.

Two-ended drift along the odometer (finite a.e. constant C(x)); solve the commutation recurrence b_{j+1}beta_j(x)=b_j beta_{j-1}(theta x); coefficients decay at both ends; normalize by the fiberwise sup to get a contraction V commuting with S with V_x K_{>=h} dense in K_{>=h-1}.
An alg(S,V,M_g)-invariant subspace is a field of tails K_{>=s(x)} with s(theta x)<=s(x)-1; strict descent on a probability space + ergodicity force s=+-inf.
alg subset {S}', so {S}' transitive; commutant lemma gives proper SOT-closed; transport to any separable H.

eureka_candidates_ranked.name: Backward intertwiner across fibers: two-ended opposite-drift weights over the odometer making a fiber-moving backward shift a bounded element of the commutant
for: It is the step that turns the HSP into a one-dimensional descent on a probability space; everything else is known (Domar fibers, decomposable operators, recurrence).

Within one fiber the backward shift is unbounded (w_{j-1}/w_j -> inf); boundedness appears only by moving to the next fiber, with the sup-normalization L(x) finite a.e. but non-integrable C(x) -- a pointwise-finiteness trick.
Syntactically tiny (opposite residue corrections +-D T_m), like Cook's extension variables, and invisible in the problem statement.

No neighbour found: searches on direct integrals of weighted shifts over ergodic transformations with commutant/hyperinvariant analysis found only Bastian 1976 (decomposition of weighted translation operators; no hyperinvariance).
If correct, it settles a problem open since ~1970 in ~10 pages, which is itself evidence of non-obviousness.
against: Commutation forces the coefficient recurrence, so once the architecture 'fibered unicellular shifts + fiber-moving commutant element' is chosen, the remaining task is a weight design; pivot distance may be short.

The architecture mirrors the known II_1-factor route (Dykema Prop 2.1: commutant of T in M contains JMJ, i.e. fiber-moving symmetries of the crossed product); the same release's companion follows that route, so BI may be a simplification of an approach already found by the model.
The drift/coboundary pattern (pointwise-finite, non-integrable transfer) is common in ergodic cocycle constructions.
No reasoning trace; discoverability cannot be probed from process.

correctness_audit.verdict: The BI argument is short and I found no gap on a full reading: the reduction (M_g-invariance -> projection field; S-invariance -> tails by the fiber criterion; V-invariance -> s(theta x)<=s(x)-1; measure preservation + ergodicity -> trivial) is sound, the drift/recurrence estimates check (increments ~ c-D=-90 per step at both ends), and V is a contraction. The deep input is the Domar-type criterion, which I did not verify line by line but which is formalized. IP is long and technical; I read every section of the main text and skimmed the appendix; no gap noticed but not verified in detail. Lean: two independent formal HSP proofs, text-level clean. Not compiled here.
checked: BI fiber weights: increments within blocks c; at block boundaries c+DN_m+D delta>=c and c+D(N_{m+1}-delta)>=c; a_0^pm=c so beta_{-1}=beta_0=e^{-c}; log w quadratic with a=c/2=5>log 3.
BI commutation: S_{theta x}V_x e_j = b_j(x) beta_{j-1}(theta x) e_j and V_x S_x e_j = beta_j(x) b_{j+1}(x) e_j agree by the recurrence.

BI decay: log b~ increments a_j(x)-a_{j-1}(theta x) ~ +c - D at positive j and -( -c + D) going down at negative j; both ends -> -inf pointwise given finitely many wraps (x not a negative integer of Z_2).
BI descent: theta F_j subset F_{j-1} subset F_j with mu preserved gives mu(F_j)=mu(E)=0.

Sanity: growth-class hyperinvariant manifolds {f: ||S^n f|| <= C rho_n} are dense here (vectors 1_E (x) e_j with E a residue class of large residue decay faster), so no obvious hyperinvariant subspace is missed; ker S = 0, ran S dense, no compact in {S}' (Lomonosov) consistent.
IP Lemma 1.3 (Dykema Prop 2.1) and Corollary 1.4 logic.
IP parameter inequality (2K+1)3e^{-L/10000} <= eps/j covers e^{-L}+2e^{-L/800}.
